rule: good. the rule line is never parsed and needs no rewrite; the work for this item is in the first two sentences, where 'ground feathers' sits inside the trigger clause.
texts: bad: as a scattered group inside the trigger, 'ground feathers' has no stable form — the translator either invents a fused ground-feather kind, which is not licensed, or must predicate 'ground' of each feather, which a rule condition cannot carry. Say the grinding as its own clause instead: "When a Keeper grinds feathers and scatters them around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern against wraiths."

bad: the entire 'whenever' condition ended up in the rule's conclusion — the only trigger left is being a Keeper — so the rule now claims every Keeper spreads ground feathers around a lit lantern and shields it, asserting the very occurrence your sentence only conditions on; 'ground feathers' as a trigger participant is the same unstable phrase as in the first sentence. Rewrite with the grinding as its own clause: "Whenever a Keeper grinds feathers and spreads them around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern against wraiths."
good. it parses as a blanket denial covering every wraith and every warded lantern, which is the natural reading, with 'warded' kept as a property of the lantern.

good. the modified bare plural becomes a fireable generic rule with 'fresh' and 'ground' both riding as conditions on the individual feather — this is the shape that works, unlike the group use in the first two sentences.

good. adjudicated faithful — the strength-zero generic rule denies warding for stale ground feathers only, and the reviewer's objection to carrying 'ground' as a property of the feather was overruled.
